The edge-case states are ready. Let me walk you through them one at a time.

**Situation 1 — a brand-new user with nothing saved yet.**
Please open **http://maker:4001/?state=empty** — this shows the app as it looks before any links exist.
*Assumption to check:* I chose to show a friendly "No links saved yet — add your first one above" message rather than a blank screen. Does that feel like the right welcome, or would you word it differently / show something else?

**Situation 2 — messy or incomplete entries.**
Please open **http://maker:4001/?state=long** — this deliberately shows two awkward links:
- One with a **very long title and very long address**. *Check:* does the way the long text wraps and stays readable look acceptable to you?
- One where I **left the title and topic blank** when saving. I made two assumptions here I'd like you to judge: when a link has **no title, I show its web address as its name** instead; and when a link has **no topic, I group it under a heading called "Untitled topic."** Do both of those fallbacks match what you'd expect, or would you handle a blank title/topic differently?

**Situation 3 — a search that finds nothing.**
Go back to the normal app at **http://maker:4001**, and in the search box type something you know isn't there, like `zzzz`.
*Check:* it shows a "No links match" message — is that the right thing to happen when a search comes up empty?

Tell me your reaction to each, and I'll then check a couple of quick behaviour questions with you in words rather than screens.
